pairs.evidence: src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_lifecycle/lifecycleView/useLifecycleView.ts:185 The Lifecycle writes the task layer it hands Athena. It names where to look (project name and id, 'Start with describe_lifecycle'), but none of its task templates states a check, and the general ask ('Help me change the development practice for {name}') has no done criterion either.

techniques.evidence: src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_lifecycle/lifecycleView/useLifecycleView.ts:185 Locate is present: the project name and id plus describe_lifecycle. The rendered en.json text is 'Help me change the development practice for {name} (id {id}). Start with describe_lifecycle.' It has no done artifact and no check. The doc-fix templates (docsAsk.ts) do state a done but also have no read-back check.

src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_lifecycle/lifecycleView/presets/docs/docsAsk.ts:24 Path lists are capped at 30, and the truncation names what it dropped (' and {count} more'). That is the 'truncation names what it dropped' rule.

src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_lifecycle/lifecycleView/presets/docs/docsAsk.ts:1 One builder for the doc-fix task family. The Next panel, FixPanel and DocsPreset all call fixDocsPrompt rather than concatenating their own text. Scope is the task layer only; Athena's own assembler owns the other layers.

pairs.registryProposal: task-envelope is scoped to delegated or dispatched calls. It does not say whether an app-composed 'Help me ...' opener sent into an interactive companion chat (a human present, the companion then acts) owes the same done and check parts. A rule for that case would settle the verdicts for UI 'ask the assistant' buttons.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/features/projects/development/goals/GoalsPage.tsx:71 The Goals page auto-sends a fixed task prompt to Athena ('Help me set up development goals for this project...'). The prompt never names the project, gives no done artifact and no check, so the model starts with nothing to locate.

techniques.evidence: src/features/projects/development/goals/GoalsPage.tsx:71 The en.json text is 'Help me set up development goals for this project. Suggest a few high-level goals based on what you know about it...'. There is no locate pointer: activeProjectId is in scope at the call site but is not interpolated. Per the rule, if there is nowhere to point, the task lacks its inputs. It also has no done shape and no check.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/db/src/repos/dev_memories.rs:240 render_for_prompt is the shared renderer for the dev-memory section that task_executor, idea_scanner, night_plan, unattended and backlog_triage inject. It drops entries that do not fit without leaving a notice in the prompt, and it reads the wall clock while rendering. Under pressure the model sees a partial memory block that presents as complete, and the ranking can change between two calls on the same corpus.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/db/src/repos/dev_memories.rs:218 Each caller passes a per-feeder character budget (900-2400), which is good. But a skipped entry leaves no '...and N not shown' line, and line 221 lets a single over-budget memory through, so the documented 'hard cap' is not hard.

src-tauri/db/src/repos/dev_memories.rs:244 Rendering reads the clock instead of taking 'now' as a declared input, so it is not pure. Decay scores move with age, at different half-lives per category, so the same corpus can render a different order or selection later. That undercuts the line 208-210 comment claiming the same corpus always renders the same block.
src-tauri/db/src/repos/dev_memories.rs:249 The section renders on its own from typed rows and returns None when there is nothing to inject, so an absent section is absent rather than an empty header.

declined.subject: prompt-assembly
declined.reason: None of the 144 files in this context assembles a model prompt. The send pipeline (athenaChatSend.ts) is not in the context, and assembly lives in the Rust companion. The words 'prompt' and 'compact' do appear, but in display senses: decision-card prompts in rosterDecisions.ts, Curator process charts counting compactions, a compact Banner prop. So absence cannot be proven lexically for a not-applicable verdict, and there is no assembly code to judge.
